questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: Personal growth and challenging myself

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Bikeable city, close proximity to Denmark for easy back and forth visits, EU, good university.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
It was a pretty cool place and I did enjoy it a lot. It is easy to get used to. 
It feels like a big city and you can tell that there is a lot more going on than just university / student life. If you are into this, I would recommend a smaller place to get really tightly knit friend groups, but it also depends on what kind of person you are.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was all very easy and they are good at keeping you informed and answering questions.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Invites to 1:1 information- and Q/A-sessions, a lot of good information by email.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I just signed up for a housing lottery and got lucky. I was staying at a "Lieven de Key" place at the Sloterdijk station, which had really good  big rooms and facilities.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Few people live on or close to campus, don't expect it! Public transport is good. Get swapfiets!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Courses were pretty easy to sign up to and the course catalogue is great. They are very nitpicky about the prerequisites, but I guess that's for our own benefit.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There is a website where you plan the semester and add the courses, taken from a list. It's a nice closed system where you don't have to worry about having misspelled the name of a course etc.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: A bit of emailing back and forth was necessary to narrow down my options.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got most of the classes I wanted except for one Robotics course for which the AI students had priority. I found something else and still got my 30 credits.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I can't really say anything interesting here. There is nothing unusual about it, you will make it. They are lenient with things, just communicate with them.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: 4/5 courses were great, that gives 4 stars.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: They were on par with UCPH courses except for 1 aforementioned course. Do not take "Applied Forecasting in Complex Systems", it's so bad and lazily taught.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Also very similar. My classes were a bit smaller. I attended zero TA-sessions, they were not a big thing in the courses I took.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Wavelets
Applied Forecasting in Complex Systems
Stochastic Simulation
Complex System Simulation
Digital Twin Engineering

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Stochastic Simulation and Complex System Simulation are really cool, the first is very well taught and gives good intuition.
Wavelets was also amazing with a great lecturer (Jan Brandts)

Digital Twin Engineering is decent, and as mentioned, don't take Applied Forecasting in Complex Systems, because the lecturer (Erman Acar) is frankly terrible at communicating clearly, an impression shared by all my classmates.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Nothing major.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Nuts are cheap. Most things are cheaper. Don't go to Albert Heijn regularly because it is a bit more expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did a lot of sports! Get the "Passe Partout Flex" membership and you can do a lot of cool stuff at the many university facilities.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was a "Dutch Culture Night" which was cheap and fun to attend.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Beer drinking and weed smoking with peers to really connect. Get someone to teach you proper weed etiquette if you are a beginner like me.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Do bike trips to the north, go to the climbing park in the forest to the south, bike to the ocean in the west, go to the nature reserve in the east (Hooge Veluwe)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy! Don't worry.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be brave and approach them. You are automatically interesting as an exchange student.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None at all, they are so similar to us.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Brutal honestly, direct communication

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Do it!
Do it!
Do it!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: love <3

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Missing cool nature.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer:
Take initiative!
Be brave!
You are so awesome for even considering this!
It will open your mind and challenge you in the best way.
I have found this to be the fastest way to grow as a person.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
